ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected in eu-west-1 by LB-health-manager at 2026-03-15T09:12:03Z. Auto traffic-shift triggered to us-east-1 (initial plan: 30% -> 60%). Symptoms: intermittent DNS resolution failures, cross-region LB health checks timing out, and a subset of backends reporting KV cache errors. Paging on-call: @Alex R (primary).

pagerduty: Paging Alex R (on-call) — please acknowledge. Trigger: SEV2 - multi-region failover abnormal.

Alex R: ack. I'm on it. Looking at LB metrics and route53 weighted records.

Alex R: quick snapshot: eu-west-1 5xx spiked to ~18% starting 09:10. Auto-shift shows traffic stuck ~58% us-east-1, but eu-west still receiving large portion and returning 502/504s.

Sam T: I see a lot of `health_check: timeout` on the regional NLB logs. Possible upstream peering issues.

Jing W: confirmed in infra metrics — cross-region interconnect showing packet loss between eu-west-1 AZ-b and backbone for ~3m.

Alex R: trying `curl -v https://api.redwood-eu.example/health` from us-east to eu-west LB:
```
* Connected to eu-west-lb (10.10.10.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake... ok
* HTTP/2 502
* read: Connection reset by peer
```

Alex R: health checks are flapping. Route53 weighted failover should have completed but I think clients/edge resolvers have cached old A records -> sticky connections into failed AZ.

Kiran: Is streaming affected? Any customers on Dedicated in EU?

CS-Bot: Alert: 7 active Dedicated customers in eu-west-1 are showing elevated errors, two on paid SLAs. CS ops team notified.

Maria C: I'm joining. If traffic-shift didn't complete, maybe the cloud provider's LB didn't drain as expected. Check drain timeout and connection re-use settings.

Alex R: Drain timeout on eu-west NLB set to 300s. But health checks keep flipping healthy/unhealthy causing inconsistent routing weights. Also seeing DNS TTL 60s but some resolvers still honoring older caches.

Sam T: I can temporarily force failover by updating Route53 policy to failover routing (set primary -> us-east) and lower TTL to 30s. That will be manual.

Jing W: Provider peering team says there's an ongoing fiber maintenance affecting eu-west AZ-b -> backbone between 09:08-09:40. They say it should be resolved soon.

Alex R: Manual plan: 1) Reduce TTL to 30s; 2) Set Route53 weighted to 0/100 (eu-west -> 0, us-east -> 100) to force shift; 3) Increase NLB drain timeout to 60s to allow connections to finish; 4) Update health-check path to /healthz?fast to avoid slow backend checks.

Maria C: I can execute the Route53 change and TTL; Alex, can you change health-check path? Sam, coordinate with provider. I'll update CS and set comms.

Sam T: Provider acknowledged partial restoration at 09:20 UTC. But DNS caching still causing ~25% of requests to hit eu-west for another 6-8 minutes.

Alex R: Pushing health-check config now: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-health-check --target-group-arn arn:... --health-check-path /healthz?fast --interval 10 --timeout 3 --healthy-threshold 2 --unhealthy-threshold 2`

Alex R: Health checks now much faster, but some older TCP sessions remain pinned. We need to force route change to 0/100.

Maria C: Route53 update done at 09:22:11 UTC: set weight eu-west=0, us-east=100, TTL=30.

ops-bot: :information_source: Automation: Traffic-shift runbook step executed by Maria C at 2026-03-15T09:22:11Z.

Kiran: Noted. CS-team posted an interim message to impacted customers at 09:23:05 UTC.

CS-Bot: Customer update: We are routing traffic to us-east while we investigate; some requests may see transient errors. Engineers are working on restoring full capacity in eu-west.

Alex R: Monitoring: error rate in eu-west falling from 18% -> 6% over 6 minutes. Global error rate dropped to ~3%. But some sessions still fail for streaming use-cases.

Jing W: Provider confirms full peering restored at 09:28 UTC. We should see caches expire around 09:30-09:35.

Sam T: I see the traffic shift finishing ~09:31:12 (us-east ~100%). Good. Still a handful of backends in eu-west showing unhealthy due to KV cache evictions that need a restart.

Alex R: I'll restart the affected backend ASGs in eu-west to clear the cache. Rolling restart started at 09:33.

Maria C: Handoff: I need to step out at 09:40 for a scheduled meeting. Alex, can you take incident lead for the rest? Alex R: taking lead.

Alex R: Restart complete at 09:38. eu-west backends healthy. Running synthetic checks now.

Alex R: Synthetic p95 latency stable, 5xx < 0.5% global. Streaming error counts down to baseline.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT RESOLVED at 2026-03-15T09:41:00Z. Summary: partial provider peering disruption in eu-west AZ-b caused health-check timeouts and DNS caching to keep traffic pinned to degraded endpoints. Automated traffic-shift partly applied but required manual Route53 failover to complete. Mitigations: forced routing to us-east, lowered TTL, adjusted health-checks, rolling restart of affected backends.

Alex R: Customer impact: ~12% of requests in EU window saw 5xx for ~18 minutes. 2 Dedicated customers experienced elevated errors and were notified. No PII exposed.

Maria C: Post-incident actions: 1) Add explicit runbook step to force Route53 failover when auto-shift stalls; 2) Reduce default TTL during failover windows; 3) Add a guard in traffic-shift automation to detect DNS caching stalls and escalate; 4) Update on-call playbook for handoffs (include exact timestamps and runbook checklist).

Kiran: Also recommend adding active BGP-peering health monitor and provider SLA review.

CS-Bot: CS follow-up: CS will schedule one-on-one updates with impacted customers and offer credits where applicable.

Alex R: Logging note: saved NLB logs and health-check history to s3://redwood-incident-archives/2391234567/ for postmortem.

ops-bot: :memo: Postmortem owner assigned: Maria C. Initial draft due 2026-03-17.

CS-Bot: Closing customer comms loop once postmortem published.

Alex R: Thanks team. I'll file the incident with timeline and attach graphs.

Maria C: thanks everyone :thumbsup:

pagerduty: Incident ticket auto-closed at 2026-03-15T09:45:00Z (status: resolved).
